title: Ben Babi

paragraphs: [The beginning of chapter 5 of Shekalim](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Shekalim.5.1) mentions him as the official in charge of the pekia. [Bartenura explains](https://www.sefaria.org/Bartenura_on_Mishnah_Shekalim.5.1.10) that he was charged with flogging priests found asleep at their posts. [The Jerusalem Talmud explains](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shekalim.5.1.16) the office as responsibility for the wicks of the menorah and the water-drawing celebration. Hyman gives Ben Babi as the reading of the Western Mishnah and Ben Bibai as the reading at [Yoma 23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.23a.9-10).

notes.text: The supplied locator reads beginning of chapter8. The office list is actually at Mishnah Shekalim5:1. Hyman gives different explanations of pekia: corporal discipline or responsibility for wicks. The malformed commentator siglum הרע״כ is rendered Bartenura in that context. The locator difference remains open.

No new primary scalar was supplied. The earlier Mishnah Shekalim 5:1 office-list consultation is inherited beside supplied רפ״ח, beginning of chapter 8. A matching chapter does not prove he/chet print or transcription history, and that proposed correction is not adopted as printed text. The malformed commentator siglum הרע״כ is shown and its Bartenura reading remains contextual. Pekia is explained by Hyman through competing discipline and wick duties, rather than silently selected as one settled office. Ben Babi/Bibai and the Western Mishnah/Yoma references remain attributed; no new identity or variants-work collation is claimed.

Hyman’s print reads רפ״ה, the beginning of chapter 5, and הרע״ב, the abbreviation for R’ Ovadiah of Bartenura. The supplied Hebrew has רפ״ח and הרע״כ. Mishnah Shekalim 5:1 has the consonants בן בבי, vocalized Ben Bevai in the consulted edition. Bartenura mentions Levites as well as priests, and cites the Jerusalem Talmud for the wick interpretation. At Yoma 23a Abaye first takes pekia to mean wicks, then changes his mind after hearing a teaching about lashes. Hyman’s specific Western Mishnah witness remains uncollated.
